result.topic_en: Main steps for solving the inverse problem of recovering a planetary orbit (its eccentricity, inclination, node and eccentric anomaly) from the ellipse into which it projects and the projected position of its focus.
result.transcription:
# # #

Die Hauptmomente der Auflösung der umgekehrten Aufgabe: aus der Projection einer Planetenbahn und ihres Brennpunkts, jene selbst zu finden sind folgende:

Es sei $\alpha$ die halbe grosse $6$[?] die halbe kleine Axe der Projectionsellipse; ferner vom Mittelpunkt der Ellipse an gerechnet, gegen eine willkürliche Abscissenlinie
$P$ .... [-Neigung-] {+Richtg+} von $\alpha$
$Q$ .... Neigung der Linie zum Brennpunkt deren Grösse $=\delta$
Man setze $\mathrm{tg}(R-P).\mathrm{tg}(Q-P) = -\frac{66}{\alpha\alpha}$
$\sqrt{\left[\frac{\cos(Q-P)^2}{\alpha\alpha}+\frac{\sin(Q-P)^2}{66}\right]} = \frac{1}{q}$
$\sqrt{\left(\frac{\cos(R-P)^2}{\alpha\alpha}+\frac{\sin(R-P)^2}{66}\right]} = \frac{1}{r}$
also $\frac{qq}{rr} = -\frac{\sin 2(R-P)}{\sin 2(Q-P)}$
[-$e = \sqrt{(1-\frac{\delta\delta}{qq})}$-][?]
$e = \frac{\delta}{q}$
$\frac{qq}{rr}.(1-ee) = -\frac{\sin 2(R-\Omega)}{\sin 2(Q-\Omega)}$
$q\cos(Q-\Omega) = a\cos E$
$q\sin(Q-\Omega) = a\cos i.\sin E$
$\frac{r}{\sqrt{(1-ee)}}.\cos(R-\Omega) = -a\sin E$
$\frac{r}{\sqrt{1-ee}}.\sin(R-\Omega) = a\cos i\cos E$
$qq+\frac{rr}{1-ee} = aa(1+\cos i^2)$
$\frac{qr}{\sqrt{(1-ee)}}\sin(R-Q) = aa\cos i$
$\frac{qr}{\sqrt{(1-ee)}}\cos(R-Q) = -\frac{1}{2}aa\sin i^2\sin 2E$
$qq-\frac{rr}{1-ee} = aa\sin i^2\cos 2E$

$aa\sin i^2.\cos(Q+R-2\Omega) = (qq+\frac{rr}{1-ee})\cos(R-Q)$
$aa\sin i^2\sin(Q+R-2\Omega) = (qq-\frac{rr}{1-ee})\sin(R-Q)$

methods.what: Definition of the conjugate direction R via the conjugate-diameter condition of the projected ellipse
Polar-form radius of the ellipse in direction Q (semi-diameter q)
Polar-form radius of the ellipse in direction R (semi-diameter r)
Ratio of the squared conjugate semi-diameters
Eccentricity from the focal distance, since the projection preserves ratios along a line
Relation determining the node direction Omega
Projection of the conjugate semi-diameters in terms of a, i, E and Omega
Sum of squares relation giving a and i
Relations for the eccentric anomaly E
